Company Description

KPFF Special Projects Division

Since 1996, KPFF's Special Projects Division has been at the forefront of addressing specialized challenges in project development. With over 150 team members in three offices strategically located in Seattle, WA, Tacoma, WA, and Long Beach, CA, our approach combines dedicated project managers, a skilled technical team, and a commitment to innovation. We offer a comprehensive range of services including civil, structural, and mechanical engineering, machinery design, construction and project management, and planning services.

We specialize in the management and design of heavy civil, structural, industrial, and waterfront infrastructure projects across the United States. Our team thrives on solving unique, multi-disciplinary challenges, collaborating closely with clients such as the Ports of Long Beach, Los Angeles, Tacoma, and Seattle, as well as various municipalities and gvernment agencies.

Join us at KPFF Special Projects Division and be part of a dynamic team driving innovation and excellence in project delivery.

Job Description

KPFF’s Special Projects Division in downtown Seattle, Washington, is seeking a full-time Project Coordinator with a minimum of five years of relevant experience to contribute to our engineering, project management, and construction management projects. In this role, you will support Principals, Project Managers, design teams, and construction management teams to help deliver projects within scope, schedule, and budget.

This position supports all phases of project delivery, from schematic design through construction and closeout, by providing project coordination, contract administration, project accounting, and administrative and business development support.

What You Will Be Doing

With minimal supervision and guidance, responsibilities may include:

Project Coordination

Assist with project controls, assisting in project scope, schedule, and budget monitoring
Set up new project files, maintain files throughout the project lifecycle, and archive closed projects
Develop and maintain project schedules and communicate key milestones
Schedule project meetings, prepare agendas and meeting notes, and track action item lists
Coordinate construction support activities, including shop drawing/submittal reviews and RFI routing
Coordinate project deliverables, QA/QC activities, and communication with clients and subconsultants
Prepare and/or finalize reports, memorandums, and technical documents
Act as the point-of-contact for project managers as needed

Contract Administration

Prepare, review, and oversee contracts, amendments, subconsultant agreements, and task orders
Track certificates of insurance and contractual compliance requirements
Assist with the creation and compilation of fee estimates and level of efforts
Finalize and execute Work Directives/Task Orders and perform contract administrative management

Project Accounting

Set up and manage spreadsheets for cost tracking and billing
Monitor contract expenditures, report variances, and assist in monthly invoicing
Prepare and review client invoices and progress reports
Respond to budget, invoice, and contract inquiries from KPFF staff, clients, and subconsultants

Group Administration

Develop and maintain MS Word and Excel templates to support business development and group operations
Support development of financial tracking tools and reports
Conduct research in active and potential market sectors
Support the development of promotional and business development materials

Qualifications

What we are looking for:

Effective communicator: verbal and written, tailored to collaborative project environments
Proactive thinker: anticipates the needs of project managers and design teams
Critical thinker: exercises independent decision-making and problem-solving
Continuous learner: approaches professional growth with humility and curiosity
Collaborative Team player: thrives in a collaborative, high-performing culture

Position Requirements

Minimum 5 years of experience in project coordination, project administration or a related role
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, SharePoint, MS Project, Bluebeam, and Smartsheet
Experience with accounting, invoicing, billing, and contract administration
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple concurrent tasks and deadlines
Superior verbal and written communication skills
Ability to work independently while supporting multiple levels of professional staff.
Professional demeanor, positive attitude, and self-motivated work ethic.

Desired Qualifications

Experience in the AEC field / design-build / engineering environment
Experience with public-sector contracting and invoicing procedures
Experience with construction documents, including plans and specifications
Technical writing certification and/or experience

Additional Information

Physical Demands And Work Environment

Duties are primarily conducted in a standard office setting, requiring prolonged periods of sitting at a desk.
Occasionally may be required to lift objects weighing up to 15 lbs.
Occasionally visiting project locations and performing indoor/outdoor field observations, which may involve walking, standing, kneeling, climbing stairs/ladders and navigating uneven terrain.

Culture And Benefits

Join KPFF for a career adventure that celebrates your expertise and fuels your development. Here, autonomy and innovation converge, empowering you to tackle complex challenges and blossom into a consulting trailblazer. Our culture fosters teamwork, ownership, and common values, ensuring that your accomplishments are celebrated and your career trajectory is in your hands. At KPFF, we're not just coworkers; we're a vibrant community fueled by collaborative creativity, offering you the chance to leave a lasting mark on pioneering projects.

Brief Description

Kidwell is seeking an experienced, motivated professional to join our team as a Low Voltage Estimator/Project Coordinator in our Lincoln or Omaha location. This position is responsible for preparing accurate, timely project proposals and providing project coordination support for Kidwell’s partnering electrical contractors, general contractors, and low voltage customers. The ideal candidate will collaborate with Kidwell’s field staff, pre-sales engineering team, vendors, partners, and customers to develop professional, accurate estimates and coordinate Integrated Systems and Phone System projects from proposal through execution.

Kidwell Core Values

At Kidwell, our core values define who we are and guide the way we work every day. Led by passion, we believe our work contributes to something bigger than ourselves. We take pride in our creativity and in delivering effective solutions that bring lasting value to our customers. Our employees act like owners, take initiative, and are treated like family. We are relentless in our pursuit of excellence, with a strong foundation of work ethic, accountability, and teamwork.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Prepare accurate, timely, and comprehensive estimates and quotes, including scope review, take-offs, pricing, proposal development, estimate reviews, change orders, and project closeout support.
Collaborate with pre-sales and field engineering teams to develop proposals that accurately reflect labor, materials, project scope, customer requirements, and implementation needs.
Coordinate with Kidwell’s vendors and partners to identify, source, order, and track equipment and materials needed for successful low voltage and phone system project installations.
Prepare detailed cost estimates for low voltage projects, including structured cabling, phone and voice systems, fiber optics, security, access control, nurse call, and audio-visual systems.
Provide project coordination for assigned low voltage and phone system projects, including planning, scheduling, implementation coordination, resource coordination, execution, and follow-up.
Support service contract renewals by preparing renewal information, coordinating required updates, and assisting with customer follow-up as needed.
Serve as a primary point of contact for clients, general contractors, subcontractors, vendors, internal project teams, and engineering teams.
Track project budgets, change orders, RFIs, submittals, and schedules to support on-time, on-budget project delivery.
Recommend improvements to estimating and phone system project coordination processes to reduce discrepancies between estimated and actual project costs.

Key Skills

Analytical Thinking: Ability to understand complex projects, customer needs, scopes of work, requested materials, and required timelines. Able to interpret written scopes and designs, ask clarifying questions, and identify potential gaps or uncertainties.
Problem Solving: Identifies and resolves issues in a timely manner, gathers and analyzes information effectively, develops alternative solutions, and uses sound judgment in challenging situations.
Oral Communication: Communicates clearly and professionally, listens actively, asks thoughtful questions, responds well to feedback, and contributes effectively in meetings and group discussions.
Written Communication: Writes clearly and accurately, adapts communication style to the audience, presents numerical data effectively, and reads and interprets written information with attention to detail.
Teamwork: Balances individual and team responsibilities, welcomes feedback, contributes to a positive team environment, supports team goals, and helps build strong working relationships.
Planning and Organization: Prioritizes tasks, plans work effectively, uses time efficiently, and manages multiple initiatives while maintaining accuracy and follow-through.

Do You Have What It Takes?

Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree in a related field, or 2+ years of low voltage experience and/or training.
Proficiency with Microsoft Outlook, Excel, and Word, with the ability and willingness to learn estimating-specific software and related programs.
Strong technical aptitude and a desire to continue learning, with the ability to understand the estimating process and adapt as business needs evolve.

Benefits

Kidwell offers competitive benefits including health insurance, dental & vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, 401K, paternity/maternity leave, and paid vacation and sick leave- Along with several employee perks including company-sponsored social events, wellness program, training, and tuition reimbursement.

Duties

This IT Data Management Journey position provides an essential opportunity to lead the SEA Program’s geospatial data management, spatial database administration, and GIS application development efforts that support statewide shoreline, shorelands, and coastal hazard work. In this role, you will manage and modernize the program’s spatial data infrastructure—designing database schemas, administering enterprise geodatabases, automating ETL workflows, and delivering authoritative datasets that underpin regulatory decisions, environmental analyses, and Coastal Atlas functionality. You will serve as the program’s primary technical authority for spatial data systems, ensuring data accuracy, consistency, and interoperability across Ecology, local governments, Tribes, and federal partners.

You will also develop and maintain Coastal Atlas applications and data services, conduct advanced spatial analyses, and support coastal and environmental models that inform statewide planning and regulatory processes. By building tools, documentation, training, and data workflows, you will strengthen staff and partner capacity to use geospatial information effectively and promote consistent, defensible environmental decision making. As the SEA Program’s primary geospatial specialist, you will play a central role in shaping data standards, improving workflow efficiency, and enhancing the accessibility of critical shoreline and coastal data used by planners, regulators, researchers, and the public.

Conduct advanced spatial analyses and develop automated spatial modeling workflows using Python, R, and ArcGIS tools to support coastal hazard assessments, ecological analyses, regulatory decisions, and resilience initiatives.
Lead the design and implementation of ETL workflows that integrate multisource datasets from local governments, Tribes, federal agencies, scientific models, and enterprise systems, ensuring seamless, accurate, and standardized data delivery.

Duties

In this role, you will collect and process credible stream hydrology information for river systems or basins that are reliable, accurate and timely. You will possess and demonstrate the skills required to install and operate stream gages in the assigned geographical area. You will also evaluate and develop rating curves, reviewing data for completeness and overall quality and providing field support to keep stations on-line and reporting accurate information.

What You Will Do

Using sound scientific principles, select measurement points that are representative of the measurement of stream discharge.
Develop individual state discharge rating curves for each measurement site by taking flow measurements that define this relationship over the entire flow regime.
Carry out cross section measurements at individual measurement sites so that accurate calculations can confirm the stage discharge rating curves developed.
Track the change in channel cross-section over time and adjust the stage-discharge rating table.
Install, operate and maintain water stage height telemetry systems.
Download data loggers and service telemetry systems and/or making upgrades as necessary.
Act as a resource to other agencies and groups that require technical assistance in regards to stream discharge measurement.

The Geologic Mapping and Paleontology Program of the Utah Geological Survey (UGS) is seeking a full time permanent Preparator – Field Paleontologist. This is a unique opportunity to build a career focused on Field Paleontology in Utah. This position will be focused on fulfilling Utah paleontology regulation regarding the documentation, preservation, and promotion of Utah’s vast paleontological resource. Funded by UGS base funding supplemented by Federal projects at multiple scales including projects for NPS, BLM, USFS, and Statemap. The incumbent will be responsible for overseeing paleontological field work and the preparation lab for a variety of paleontological projects with a focus on resource inventory, salvage, and research in support of understanding Utah’s geological history and stratigraphic framework. Maintenance of Utah’s ever growing Paleontological Locality Database is a critical part of the program and with 25,000 records it is unrivaled anywhere.

Key Responsibilities

Key responsibilities and day to day responsibilities of this position:

Oversee fossil preparation in UGS preparation lab by insuring equipment is operational, preparing significant fossils, overseeing volunteers, organizing the transfer of prepared specimens into appropriate repositories. Supervise paleontological field work by overseeing base camp operations, excavations, volunteers, collecting field data, and creating digital paleontological locality files.
Perform geologic field work that includes putting paleontological field data into geological context stratigraphically and geographically.
Prepare paleontological permit applications, supporting materials, and final reports for federal and state agencies as needed working with State Paleontologist.
Review paleontological reports and publications for UGS, external scientists, and students. Address review comments and complete reports on time for contract deliverables, provide timely reviews of geologic publications in collaboration with other UGS staff and outside geoscientists.
Work closely with the State Paleontologist to address issues related to paleontological resource management on public lands.

Collaborate with other Utah Geological Survey staff and external scientists investigating the geological heritage of Utah.

B.S. in Geology or Biology (Paleontology) required; M.S. or Ph.D. in Geology or Biology (Paleontology) is preferred.

Experience in both paleontological inventory investigations and overseeing large scale vertebrate fossil excavations.

This IT Data Management Journey position provides an essential opportunity to lead the SEA Program’s geospatial data management, spatial database administration, and GIS application development efforts that support statewide shoreline, shorelands, and coastal hazard work. In this role, you will manage and modernize the program’s spatial data infrastructure—designing database schemas, administering enterprise geodatabases, automating ETL workflows, and delivering authoritative datasets that underpin regulatory decisions, environmental analyses, and Coastal Atlas functionality. Conduct advanced spatial analyses and develop automated spatial modeling workflows using Python, R, and ArcGIS tools to support coastal hazard assessments, ecological analyses, regulatory decisions, and resilience initiatives.

Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen

The Department of Ecology is hiring a Streamflow Hydrologist
(Hydrogeologist 2) within the Environmental Assessment Program .

Location:

Central Region Office in Union Gap, WA .
Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the duty station.

Schedule

Apply by July 30, 2026

Duties

In this role, you will collect and process credible stream hydrology information for river systems or basins that are reliable, accurate and timely. You will possess and demonstrate the skills required to install and operate stream gages in the assigned geographical area. You will also evaluate and develop rating curves, reviewing data for completeness and overall quality and providing field support to keep stations on-line and reporting accurate information.

What You Will Do

Using sound scientific principles, select measurement points that are representative of the measurement of stream discharge.
Develop individual state discharge rating curves for each measurement site by taking flow measurements that define this relationship over the entire flow regime.
Carry out cross section measurements at individual measurement sites so that accurate calculations can confirm the stage discharge rating curves developed.
Track the change in channel cross-section over time and adjust the stage-discharge rating table.
Install, operate and maintain water stage height telemetry systems.
Download data loggers and service telemetry systems and/or making upgrades as necessary.
Act as a resource to other agencies and groups that require technical assistance in regards to stream discharge measurement.

Teamwork & Collaboration – Ability to work respectfully and cooperatively with others to support shared goals and maintain productive working relationships.

Field Operations – Ability to plan, prepare for, and conduct fieldwork safely and effectively to collect accurate environmental data.
Hydrologic Measurement & Analysis - Ability to measure stream flow and channel characteristics to develop and update accurate stage-discharge rating curves.
Data Quality & Management – Ability to record, review, and maintain accurate data and notes to ensure data integrity and support scientific analyses. Ability to enter, validate, and analyze data using databases and standard office software to support accurate reporting.
Equipment & Vehicle Operation – Ability to safely operate field equipment, tools, vehicles, and/or boats to access sites and maintain monitoring stations.

Education:
involving a major study in hydrogeology, hydrology, geology or closely allied field.

a Master’s degree or higher.
